SF.summary:
- **Christian McCaffrey (RB)** — He got plenty of work in the first camp practice and looked “just fine” coming off last season’s heavy workload, with a handful of carries and good rhythm with Brock Purdy. Jordan James appears to be next up in the backfield, with Kaelon Black and Patrick Taylor Jr. behind him, which gives James the clearest early handcuff signal behind McCaffrey. [5, 8]

- **Kurtis Rourke (QB)** — He appears to be getting the first shot at the QB3 job, while Adrian Martinez also mixed in for reps. That’s a depth-chart battle worth tracking for roster construction, even if it’s not a major fantasy spot. [5]

- **Connor Colby (OL)** — He got the first crack at left guard, with Robert Jones as the other top contender, and Foerster said the job won’t be settled until pads come on. It matters because the early favorite at LG can stabilize the interior line and indirectly support the run game. [5]

numbered_sources.title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 1: - First off, a quick reminder that pads won't come on for a few days so a little bit of a caveat on all things until we get to the real stuff. - Coach Kyle Shanahan came out to the field after a couple of team periods and stood by GM John Lynch for much of the next half hour or so. Shanahan was wearing sunglasses to cover the black eyes he has from his accident with LB Fred Warner complimenting him on his "disguise." Warner, FB Kyle Juszczyk and LB Dre Greenlaw all came out to greet Shanahan during a special teams period with Shanahan heading back inside before practice ended. - The only player not participating to start the roughly 90-minute session was DB Nate Hobbs. It's unclear what the issue is there, though he had some knee problems last year that limited him. - OT Vederian Lowe and WR Christian Kirk seemed to get shaken up during the practice. Lowe was having his right ankle looked at after going down on an early snap in team drills. - OL coach Chris Foerster is handling some additional head coaching responsibilities right now but downplayed how much more he has to do. He did say some of the little things like whether to run a rep over again if someone jumps offsides are little things he has to think about that he normally doesn't. He will also be handling the news conferences until Shanahan returns. - In terms of some positional battles, a few things stood out: Connor Colby is getting the first crack at left guard. He and Robert Jones are the top contenders but it was all Colby on Sunday. Foerster said that is earned by his incumbent status but nothing will be solidified until pads come on and evaluations can take place. - It looks like there will be a battle again at safety. Marques Sigle and Ji'Ayir Brown were first up with Malik Mustapha rotating a bit with Sigle in this practice. Sigle had an interception on a ball thrown right to him by QB Mac Jones and Mustapha later had a nice PBU on a deep ball intended for WR Ricky Pearsall. - SAM linebacker is an interesting spot that also figures to have multiple players getting a look but Nick Martin appears to be getting a real shot. He was in with Warner and Greenlaw in the few base defensive packages the Niners ran on Sunday. - Plenty of work for RB Christian McCaffrey today and he looks to be just fine as he comes off the heavy workload of last season. He got a handful of carries and he and QB Brock Purdy were in good rhythm. On one play, McCaffrey got isolated against rookie pass rusher Romello Height. McCaffrey got free and hauled it in for a would-be big gain. - Jordan James appears to be next up after McCaffrey with Kaelon Black and Patrick Taylor Jr. after that. Some good stuff from James in run game and catching passes. But again, early, and we'll see how that continues to play out. - A strong day out of the gate for Purdy. I had him at 10-of-12 on the day with the highlight coming on a deep ball down the left side for a big gain to WR Mike Evans. Evans created space with a good release against CB Deommodore Lenoir for the completion. - A bit more of a struggle for Jones, who threw the interception to Sigle and also had a pass he attempted to layer over the middle get deflected and intercepted by LB Jalen Graham. Jones rebounded a bit later by hitting rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling for a big gain and then finding Stribling again to wrap up the session. - Kurtis Rourke appears to be getting the first shot at the QB3 job with Adrian Martinez getting a few reps, too. - Some early signs of the Raheem Morris effect on the defense as the Niners are already toying with 5-man fronts. It should be no secret that's something that intend to do more and Trent Williams and Warner talked openly about it a bit after practice. Some interesting combinations being thrown out there as the Niners begin to install those looks. - TE George Kittle is on PUP but came out during practice to watch team drills and chat up John Lynch. Also saw Isaac Guerendo doing the same and DT Alfred Collins do an extensive workout on the side. Again, Collins seems to be on the quickest timeline to return. - Among those getting return opportunities during special teams period: Junior Bergen, Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, Will Pauling. - That'll do it for today. Welcome back everyone. Back again tomorrow from Bay Area Stadium, er, uh, Levi's (I think we are allowed to call it that again).

Crisp first training camp practice for the 49ers. Some highlights, including... 🏈a Brock Purdy deep heave to Mike Evans, big gain 🏈Malik Mustapha explosive PBU against Ricky Pearsall on another great ball from Purdy 🏈De'Zhaun Stribling made a couple nice catches, including one on a deep out and then one down the seam to close practice 🏈Fred Warner swarmed in for a "welcome back" tackle on Play 3 — was fired up 🏈CMC beat Romello Height, who was dropping in coverage as part of Raheem Morris' new defensive look, with nifty cutback in the flat 🏈CMC, with a lot of juice to open camp, also later caught a pass against the much smaller Upton Stout 🏈Jalen Graham INT off Mac Jones, which came off a Garret Wallow tip 🏈Kyle Shanahan half-hour cameo

DAL.summary:
- **Phil Mafah (RB)** — Dallas wants to keep Javonte Williams fresh, and Mafah is a candidate to handle more of the goal-line work after scoring a short TD in the season finale. That gives him a clearer touchdown-oriented path and makes him the back to watch for emerging fantasy utility if the role grows. [4]

- **Michael Trigg / Luke Schoonmaker (TE)** — Jake Ferguson has a firm grasp on the starting job, but the depth chart behind him is unsettled, with offseason hype building around undrafted free agent Michael Trigg and Luke Schoonmaker potentially fighting for his roster spot. That matters mainly in deep formats, but it’s the clearest TE usage battle in camp. [1]

- **Sam Howell / Joe Milton (QB)** — Howell and Milton are set to battle in camp and preseason for the primary backup role behind Dak Prescott. It’s not a standard fantasy starter job, but it matters for contingency value and which passer would be next up if Prescott missed time. [1]

- **Tyler Guyton / Nathan Thomas (OT)** — Left tackle is one of Dallas’ biggest camp questions, with Guyton trying to hold off Thomas for the starting job. It’s not directly fantasy-relevant, but better protection would support Prescott and the overall passing game. [1]

- **Kimani Vidal (RB)** — He was described as a sleeper cut or trade candidate if Keaton Mitchell stays healthy. That’s a direct warning sign for Vidal’s touch outlook and suggests Mitchell could gain backfield relevance if he holds up. [1]

- **David Njoku (TE)** — The tight end pecking order is unsettled after Njoku’s late arrival; the note says he’d slot above Charlie Kolar at a minimum, and another item had Oronde Gadsen as the “locked-in” No. 1 before Njoku entered the mix. That keeps the target and red-zone distribution in flux, with Njoku the most fantasy-relevant TE to monitor. [1, 7]

PHI.summary:
- **Eagles offense** — Philadelphia finished 30th in the league in average third-down distance at 7.5 yards in the 2025 regular season. That’s a rough efficiency backdrop for the offense and suggests more difficult drive sustainability, but no specific player usage change is specified. [5]

- **Marcus Epps (S)** — The Eagles are content with Epps as the starting safety opposite Andrew Mukuba heading into training camp, and they’re okay if he opens the season in that role. It matters because this is the clearest current answer at a starting spot, even though the team could still look to upgrade it during camp. [4]

- **Riq Woolen (CB)** — Woolen was singled out as one of the spring standouts and as a high-level corner who raises the ceiling of the secondary alongside Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean. That’s a meaningful defensive boost for Philadelphia, but it doesn’t move fantasy roles directly. [2]
